audits.title: Clinical audit investigating the recognition of tardive dyskinesia in an acute inpatient setting
audits.standard: AIMS assessment every 3–6 months for patients on antipsychotics
audits.setting: Ward 4, Becklin Centre, male acute psychiatric ward, Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 3/33 (9.1%) on antipsychotics over three months had an AIMS assessment; 14 (28.0%) given verbal information on EPSEs; 19 (38.0%) had documented side-effect assessment.

audits.other_findings: Only 12 (24.0%) received information about wider side effects; education of the medical workforce proposed.
audits.citation: Romeu D, Elisha-Aboh C, Abid H, Merry L, Mahmood T, Lacey F. Clinical audit investigating the recognition of tardive dyskinesia in an acute inpatient setting. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S101-S102.

audits.title: Clinical Audit on the Measurement of Antipsychotic Side Effects Using Rating Scales (GASS, LUNSERS, and SESCAM) in Community Settings
audits.standard: NICE guidelines and Trust policy on monitoring of psychotropic medications: side effects assessed with a recommended rating scale (GASS, LUNSERS or SESCAM) at three months and one year after starting antipsychotics
audits.setting: Two community mental health teams, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: No rating scales used (0%) at three months or one year; side effects documented informally in case notes in 96%

cycle2.result: Use of an objective rating scale improved to 24%

audits.other_findings: Extrapyramidal side effects were the most documented side effects in both cycles; uptake of scales remained far from ideal.
audits.citation: Sodiya O, Adegoke A, Ilinoiu G, Morgans C. Clinical Audit on the Measurement of Antipsychotic Side Effects Using Rating Scales (GASS, LUNSERS, and SESCAM) in Community Settings. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S182-S183.

audits.title: Assessing Adherence: Audit of Glasgow Antipsychotic Side-Effect Scale Completion for Patients on Antipsychotic Depot Injections at Guildford CMHRS SABP
audits.standard: Trust guideline: GASS completed at 12 weeks and 6 months after initiation, annually thereafter and at each dose titration
audits.setting: Guildford community mental health recovery service, Surrey and Borders Partnership

cycle1.result: GASS conducted in 8 cases (26.6%); 7 (23.3%) within the last year.

audits.intervention: Findings shared at the service with a recommendation for staff to use GASS at outpatient appointments and document scores on depot charts and SystmOne.

cycle2.period: Six months after the initial audit
cycle2.result: GASS completed in 16 cases (55.17%), all within the last year.

audits.other_findings: Further suggestions included refresher courses, pharmacy team adherence and motivating medical and nursing staff.
audits.citation: Singh H, Syed M, Mannali V, Sharma E. Assessing Adherence: Audit of Glasgow Antipsychotic Side-Effect Scale Completion for Patients on Antipsychotic Depot Injections at Guildford CMHRS SABP. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S169-S170. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.435.

audits.title: Completion Audit of Inpatient Glasgow Anti-Psychotic Side-Effect Scale (GASS) Forms
audits.standard: BNF minimum standards, NICE CG178 and SIGN 131: side-effect review after initiation and dose titration, at 3 months and annually (gold standard adds 1 month); GASS form completion

cycle1.result: GASS completion rate 7% across both wards; only 1 form valid; one ward had no completed forms

audits.intervention: Presentation at ward QI meetings, infographic for staff, highlighting role and importance of the forms; re-audit after 2 months

cycle2.result: Completion rate rose from 7% to 26% (3 to 9 patients); valid forms increased from 1 to 4

audits.other_findings: Improvement described as sub-optimal; patient acuity limited completion.
audits.citation: Tait A, Wong E. Completion Audit of Inpatient Glasgow Anti-Psychotic Side-Effect Scale (GASS) Forms. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S264-S265. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.636.

audits.title: Audit of depot antipsychotic side-effect monitoring within a Community Treatment Team (CTT) in the North East of England in 2022
audits.standard: NICE and local trust guidelines: 100% of patients on depot antipsychotics have a GASS form yearly; 100% have a GASS ever; completed GASS forms accessible on RiO
audits.setting: North Tyneside Community Treatment Team, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear Trust

cycle1.result: 88% had a GASS in the past year; 97% of GASS recorded on RiO.

cycle2.result: 53% had a GASS completed in the past year (red); 95% had a GASS ever (green); 98% of GASS recorded on RiO (green).

audits.other_findings: This was the fourth re-audit; the fall in yearly GASS completion was attributed to COVID-19 disruption of face-to-face reviews. Re-audit planned for 2024/25.
audits.citation: Mohamed O, Ahuja N, Siddiqui S, Aluru S, Keidan N, Eissa F, et al.. Audit of depot antipsychotic side-effect monitoring within a Community Treatment Team (CTT) in the North East of England in 2022. European Psychiatry. 2025;68(S1):S796-S797. doi:10.1192/j.eurpsy.2025.1619.

audits.title: Monitoring side-effects of antipsychotics using the glasgow antipsychotic side-effect scale
audits.standard: NICE, RCPsych and Maudsley guidance: weekly side-effect review with GASS
audits.setting: Mixed acute general adult psychiatric ward, Dorset Healthcare University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 0% compliance: no patients completed a weekly GASS.

audits.intervention: Training session for ward staff on using the GASS.
audits.other_findings: Main cause of non-completion was staff not offering the GASS; when offered, completion was 100%.
audits.citation: Sterritt J. Monitoring side-effects of antipsychotics using the glasgow antipsychotic side-effect scale. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S106-S107.

audits.title: GASS-tly side effects: antipsychotic monitoring for inpatients across NHS Lanarkshire
audits.standard: SIGN 131 and NHS Lanarkshire recommendation: GASS offered on admission and after antipsychotic initiation or titration
audits.setting: General adult psychiatry inpatients, University Hospital Hairmyres and University Hospital Wishaw, NHS Lanarkshire

cycle1.result: GASS on admission 4.2%, after initiation/titration 9.5%, discussed at MDT 3.7%.

audits.intervention: Presentations at clinical governance and departmental teaching, email to consultants, meetings with senior charge nurses, and GASS added to routine admission paperwork.

cycle2.result: GASS on admission 11.1%, after initiation/titration 40.0%, discussed at MDT 21.7%.

audits.other_findings: Improvement was modest; greater gains in prescriber-led measures.
audits.citation: Paton C, Hammond S, Hills J, Jones L, Wong E. GASS-tly side effects: antipsychotic monitoring for inpatients across NHS Lanarkshire. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S97-S97.

audits.title: Monitoring and documentation of side effects from depot antipsychotic medication: an interdisciplinary audit of practice in a regional mental health service.
audits.setting: Rural regional mental health service, East Galway (St Brigid's Hospital, Ballinasloe)

cycle1.result: Most had an annual documented medical review and prescription; injection site condition documented in 5 (8%); site alternation in 28 (47%); no written consent to treatment in any; no information on depot and side effects documented in 57 (95%).

audits.intervention: A standardised checklist was developed to be introduced by all teams (not yet re-audited).
audits.other_findings: 60 case files were 31% of the 181 service users on depots; failure to monitor some blood tests was partly due to unclear responsibility.
audits.citation: Cleary A, Walsh F, Connolly H, Hays V, Oluwole B, Macken E, et al.. Monitoring and documentation of side effects from depot antipsychotic medication: an interdisciplinary audit of practice in a regional mental health service. J Psychiatr Ment Health Nurs. 2012;19(5):395-401. doi:10.1111/j.1365-2850.2011.01807.x. PMID: 22070791.

audits.title: Audit: Monitoring of side effects using GASS (Glasgow Antipsychotic Side-Effect Scale).
audits.standard: Hospital policy requiring completion of Glasgow Antipsychotic Side-Effect Scale (GASS) forms

cycle1.result: Only 31% of patients had completed GASS forms.

audits.intervention: Remaining patients were supported to complete the forms.

cycle2.result: 92% of patients compliant with the policy.

audits.other_findings: Suitability of the form for adolescents was questioned because of sensitive side-effect items; recommended completion on admission and at regular intervals.
audits.citation: Iankov B, Prabhakar S, Rahman A, Hosseini F. Audit: Monitoring of side effects using GASS (Glasgow Antipsychotic Side-Effect Scale). Psychiatr Danub. 2017;29(Suppl 3):685-686. PMID: 28953853.

audits.title: Side-effect monitoring of continuing LAI antipsychotic medication in UK adult mental health services.
audits.setting: 62 UK adult mental health services (POMH-UK quality improvement programme)

cycle1.result: Side-effect assessment documented in the past year in 2304 (45%) cases.

audits.other_findings: Assessments were largely untargeted to the side-effect profiles of individual LAIs.
audits.citation: Paton C, Craig TKJ, McConnell B, Barnes TRE. Side-effect monitoring of continuing LAI antipsychotic medication in UK adult mental health services. Ther Adv Psychopharmacol. 2021;11:2045125321991278. doi:10.1177/2045125321991278. PMID: 33889383.
